failure_reason: The dropped/altered index did not intersect with a hot, selective predicate in the live TPC-C workload, so the optimizer still used alternative indexes (e.g., PK prefixes) and avoided full table scans. As a result, rows_examined_ratio stayed ≤ 2, EXPLAIN access_type never showed ALL, no statements breached the slow-query threshold, and the overall QPS did not drop enough to hit the 0.7 ratio_down rule. In short: the missing index was either the wrong one or not exercised by the workload at sufficient intensity/duration to propagate to poor_plan → slow_query → qps_drop.
suggested_changes: Schema (target the hot lookup): Drop the customer name index used by Payment/Order-Status to maximize rows scanned per row returned. Execute: ALTER TABLE tpcc_10W.customer DROP INDEX idx_customer_name; and drop the Orders-by-customer index: ALTER TABLE tpcc_10W.orders DROP INDEX idx_orders_cust; (use your actual index names if they differ). Then rebuild them in rollback.

Force at least one full table scan to satisfy poor_plan: Add a short-lived reporting SQL that is guaranteed to be non-sargable so EXPLAIN shows access_type=ALL, e.g.: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tpcc_10W.customer IGNORE INDEX(PRIMARY, idx_customer_name) WHERE (c_w_id + 0) = 1 AND (c_d_id + 0) = 1 AND UPPER(c_last) = 'BARROW'; Run this at a steady rate during the chaos phase.

Amplify rows_examined_ratio: Ensure the above query returns very few rows while scanning many. Using UPPER() on c_last and arithmetic on c_w_id/c_d_id disables index usage and forces a full scan. Keep LIMIT low (or no LIMIT) so rows_examined is high relative to rows returned.

Guarantee slow_query hits: Temporarily lower long_query_time for the workload sessions to 0.2s so the full scans are captured as slow queries (SET SESSION long_query_time=0.2 before issuing queries), or increase the scan query payload (e.g., remove LIMIT, add ORDER BY with filesort) so latency > 1s on tpcc_10W.

Increase workload pressure to produce a visible QPS drop: Double terminals (e.g., from 64 to 128) and reduce think time during the chaos phase. Add a scan workload at 8–12 concurrent sessions running the non-sargable COUNT(*) query continuously. This increases contention and IO, lowering throughput.

Duration and measurement windows: Run the missing_index phase for at least 600 seconds and ensure a clean 2–3 minute baseline window immediately before index drops, then a stable 5-minute post-injection window for QPS comparison to satisfy qps_ratio ratio_down 0.7.

Target a second hot path if needed: If poor_plan still shows range instead of ALL, introduce an additional scan on orders by a non-indexed predicate, e.g., SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tpcc_10W.orders IGNORE INDEX(PRIMARY, idx_orders_cust) WHERE YEAR(o_entry_d)=2020; to force a full scan and filesort/grouping.

Rollback plan: After the experiment, recreate the dropped indexes to restore normal performance: ALTER TABLE tpcc_10W.customer ADD INDEX idx_customer_name (c_w_id, c_d_id, c_last, c_first); ALTER TABLE tpcc_10W.orders ADD INDEX idx_orders_cust (o_w_id, o_d_id, o_c_id, o_id);

missing_index.sql: ALTER TABLE tpcc_10W.customer DROP INDEX idx_customer_name; ALTER TABLE tpcc_10W.orders DROP INDEX idx_orders_cust;
missing_index.rollback_sql: ALTER TABLE tpcc_10W.customer ADD INDEX idx_customer_name (c_w_id, c_d_id, c_last, c_first); ALTER TABLE tpcc_10W.orders ADD INDEX idx_orders_cust (o_w_id, o_d_id, o_c_id, o_id);

risk_warning: Dropping secondary indexes on large TPC-C tables can trigger long-running DDL and elevated IO/CPU; depending on your MySQL/InnoDB settings, it may lock writes or cause significant latency spikes. Ensure ALGORITHM/LOCK settings meet your tolerance and run during a controlled window. Lowering long_query_time globally affects all sessions—prefer SET SESSION for only the injected workload. Always restore indexes with the provided rollback_sql after the experiment.
